document.title: Usama bin Ladin: Taliban Announce Cut-Off Date for Receipt of Evidence; GOP Official Says Taliban Growing More Intransigent (Islama 08369)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] Two sources, including a Pakistani government official, say the Taliban are growing more inflexible on extraditing bin Laden. They attribute this to press reports that the Saudi Interior Minister exonerated bin Laden over Khobar Towers and Riyadh, and to the lack of U.S. evidence. The Taliban set a 20 Nov 1998 cut-off date for evidence to their Supreme Court. Excised.

"CHIEF JUSTICE" MOHAMMAD SADIQ WAS ALSO QUOTED AS STATING THAT THE PROCEEDINGS HAVE ALREADY BEGUN.

events.description: Taliban announced their 'Supreme Court' was open to receiving evidence on Bin Ladin, open-ended.
Abdul Hai Mutmain said evidence must reach court before 20 Nov or Bin Ladin would be acquitted.
Pakistani MFA official told US POLOFF the Taliban were growing intransigent.
Crown Prince Abdullah visited Lahore and expressed concern over Bin Ladin's presence in Afghanistan.
Taliban cut-off date for evidence on Bin Ladin.
Taliban announced their 'Supreme Court' was open to receiving evidence on Bin Ladin, with no cut-off date.
Crown Prince Abdullah visited Lahore in late October and expressed concern over Bin Ladin's presence in Afghanistan.
Taliban spokesman Mutmain said evidence on Bin Ladin must reach the court before Nov 20 or Bin Ladin would be acquitted.
Embassy political officer met a Pakistani MFA official who said Taliban were growing more intransigent on Bin Ladin.
Political officer met another source who agreed Taliban hardened after Nayif's reported remarks.
actors: Nayif bin Abd al-Aziz Al Saud

events.description: Taliban cut-off date for receipt of evidence on Bin Ladin by their Supreme Court.
US Embassy Islamabad cabled State urging consideration of an announcement on evidence for the Taliban.

relationships.detail: Taliban press spokesman.
relationships.quote: TALIBAN PRESS SPOKESMAN ABDUL HAI MUTMAIN

relationships.detail: Quoted as Chief Justice of the Taliban court.
relationships.quote: "CHIEF JUSTICE" MOHAMMAD SADIQ

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin present in Afghanistan under Taliban; US urged Pakistan to press Taliban to expel him.
relationships.quote: PRESS THE TALIBAN TO EXPEL BIN LADIN TO A PLACE WHERE HE CAN BE BROUGHT TO JUSTICE

relationships.detail: Pakistan has greater influence on the Taliban.
relationships.quote: IT IS PAKISTAN THAT HAS THE GREATER INFLUENCE ON THE TALIBAN

relationships.source: Nayif bin Abd al-Aziz Al Saud
relationships.detail: Reportedly cleared Bin Ladin of involvement in Khobar Towers and Riyadh bombings.
relationships.quote: SAUDI GOVERNMENT HAD CLEARED BIN LADIN OF INVOLVEMENT IN THE KHOBAR TOWERS AND RIYADH BOMBINGS

relationships.detail: The 'Supreme Court' is the Taliban's court body that is handling the Bin Ladin inquiry.
relationships.quote: EVIDENCE CONCERNING TERRORIST USAMA BIN LADIN BY THEIR "SUPREME COURT."

relationships.detail: The Taliban are conducting an inquiry into Bin Ladin via their court and say they will acquit him if no evidence arrives by Nov 20.
relationships.quote: IF BY THEN THERE IS NOTHING, WE WILL CLOSE THE CASE AND IN OUR EYES HE WILL BE ACQUITTED.

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin is present in Afghanistan, which concerned Crown Prince Abdullah.
relationships.quote: GREAT CONCERN OVER BIN LADIN'S PRESENCE IN AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin is in Afghanistan, and the Taliban are resisting expelling him.
relationships.quote: PRESS THE TALIBAN TO EXPEL BIN LADIN TO A PLACE WHERE HE CAN BE BROUGHT TO JUSTICE.

relationships.source: Nayif bin Abd al-Aziz Al Saud
relationships.detail: Nayif is the Saudi Interior Minister and described as one of the top five Saudi government leaders.
relationships.quote: NAYIF IS KNOWN TO BE ONE OF THE TOP FIVE LEADERS IN THE SAUDI GOVERNMENT.

relationships.source: Nayif bin Abd al-Aziz Al Saud
relationships.detail: Nayif was reported to have cleared Bin Ladin of involvement in the Khobar Towers and Riyadh bombings.
relationships.quote: THE SAUDI GOVERNMENT HAD CLEARED BIN LADIN OF INVOLVEMENT IN THE KHOBAR TOWERS AND RIYADH BOMBINGS

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin was reportedly exonerated of involvement in the Khobar Towers bombing.
relationships.quote: EXONERATED BIN LADIN FOR INVOLVEMENT IN THE KHOBAR TOWERS AND RIYADH BOMBINGS

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin was reportedly exonerated of involvement in the Riyadh bombing.
relationships.quote: EXONERATED BIN LADIN FOR INVOLVEMENT IN THE KHOBAR TOWERS AND RIYADH BOMBINGS

relationships.detail: Abdullah's views are cited as the Saudi government's definitive view.
relationships.quote: THE SAUDI GOVERNMENT'S DEFINITIVE VIEW ON [BIN LADIN] MATTER HAD BEEN EXPRESSED BY CROWN PRINCE ABDULLAH

relationships.detail: Abdullah visited Lahore in late October 1998 and expressed concern over Bin Ladin.
relationships.quote: DURING HIS LATE OCTOBER VISIT TO LAHORE

relationships.detail: Eastham is Deputy Chief of Mission who classified the cable.
relationships.quote: CLASSIFIED BY ALAN EASTHAM, DEPUTY CHIEF OF MISSION.

relationships.detail: The embassy cabled the Secretary of State with an action request.
relationships.quote: FM AMEMBASSY ISLAMABAD TO SECSTATE WASHDC IMMEDIATE

relationships.detail: The MFA confirmed Mutmain's remarks as accurately reflecting Taliban views.
relationships.quote: CONFIRMED BY THE PAKISTANI MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS AS ACCURATELY REFLECTING TALIBAN VIEWS

relationships.detail: The Embassy political officer was told the Taliban reasons by an MFA official.
relationships.quote: MFA, TOLD POLOFF NOVEMBER 10 THAT THE TALIBAN HAD DECIDED TO ANNOUNCE A CUT-OFF DATE

relationships.detail: The newspaper reported the court plans to collect evidence between Nov 9-20.
relationships.quote: ACCORDING TO ONE ARTICLE IN "THE FRONTIER POST," THE TALIBAN "SUPREME COURT" PLANS TO COLLECT EVIDENCE BETWEEN NOVEMBER 9-20.

relationships.detail: The Taliban were angry the US did not respond to their offer to accept evidence and did not provide any.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN WERE ANGERED THAT THE U.S. HAS NOT RESPONDED TO THEIR ANNOUNCEMENT

key_claims: The Taliban set a 20 Nov 1998 cut-off for evidence against Bin Ladin in their Supreme Court inquiry.
A Pakistani MFA official attributed Taliban hardening to reported Saudi Interior Minister Nayif statements clearing Bin Ladin.
Taliban were frustrated the US gave them no evidence and upset by the US indictment and reward offer.
The US urged Pakistan to press the Taliban to expel Bin Ladin.
Embassy judged Taliban believed Saudi Arabia had separated from the US on the matter.
